title: Arbitrary base change of semistable marked curves and fibrewise stability
statement: Let $T$ be any scheme. First, for every multipointed $T$-curve $(X,D)$ (not necessarily semistable) and every morphism $T'\to T$, the pair $(X\times_TT',D\times_TT')$ is a multipointed $T'$-curve; if moreover $T$ and $T'$ are integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and $T'\to T$ maps the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of $T'$ to that of $T$, and the generic curve of $X$ is smooth and its generic marking is etale, then the same holds for the pulled-back pair. Now let $(Y,E)$ be a semistable multipointed $T$-curve. For every morphism $T'\to T$, the pair $(Y\times_T T',E\times_T T')$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is again a semistable multipointed $T'$-curve: both structural morphisms are flat and finitely presented of pure relative dimensions $1$ and $0$, the marking is a closed immersion and etale over $T'$, the curve has only ordinary nodes in geometric fibres, and the marking lies in the relative smooth locus. The relative smooth locus pulls back to the relative smooth locus. These properties are local for an open cover of $T$. More generally, for a compatible morphism of multipointed pairs $f:(Y,E)\to(X,D)$ with semistable source, the condition that every geometric fibre of $Y$ has no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f$ and meets the marking and singular locus in at most two points is preserved by arbitrary base change and is local for open covers of $T$. This assertion concerns the geometric stability condition; it does not assert that an arbitrary base change of an $\eta$-modification is still a modification. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].
